common: Use case: stylized-concept. Deliver ONE finished opaque landscape game environment atlas, EXACTLY four independent rectangular 3:2 landscape paintings in a precise 2 by 2 equal grid. Overall landscape canvas 3:2. Edge-to-edge quadrants meet exactly at the center; no lines, gutters, frames, titles, lettering or UI. Each quadrant is its own actual traversable background map for a cozy Korean pixel RPG in a magical storybook, not a cutscene. Elevated three-quarter TOP-DOWN fixed RPG camera, near-orthographic, like carefully hand-placed 16-bit environmental pixel art. Consistent modest RPG character scale, hard-edged pixel clusters with limited harmonious palettes, deep cool contact shadows, broken highlight edges, exquisite material details, medium-scale floor pixels with grounded ambient lighting. Physical objects should be big enough to read at 450 pixels wide. Craft a real place with one beautiful landmark per map and rich botanical, architectural or material identity. Compose each playfield with a broad continuous open walkable middle from 12% to 88% panel width and from 35% to 84% panel height, including the center: richly patterned walkable ground, no giant central objects, pits, solid fences or water separating the yard. We overlay all actors, objectives and guidance in code. Tall structures and scenic mass are clustered in rear 23%, at very far side margins and a few bottom corners. Important back features must extend to 28% down the panel so they are visible below our HUD. NO skyline panorama, no horizon line, no strong perspective, camera looking DOWN at the floor. Use ground materials, low relief, sun patches and curving paths to make the open play area feel busy without littering it. No characters, people, animals, animal silhouettes, icons, portals, floating UI, speech bubbles, letters, watermarks or text anywhere. No duplicates of a scene. Depict only the backdrop; never invent plot events.
